questions.question: Which JDBC URL is correct for a PostgreSQL database named library on the local machine?
options: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/library
jdbc:postgres://localhost:3306/library
jdbc:mysql://localhost:5432/library
postgresql:localhost/library
questions.explanation: The prefix is jdbc:postgresql: and the default PostgreSQL port is 5432.

questions.question: Why does the PostgreSQL driver dependency have runtime scope?
options: It works only in production builds
It must be hidden from Maven
It replaces Hibernate at runtime
Your code never imports it, and Spring Boot only needs it when the app runs
questions.explanation: The driver is used through the JDBC API, so no source file imports its classes.

questions.question: An environment variable SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL is set to a different URL than application.properties. Which URL does the app use?
options: The file always wins
The environment variable wins
Spring Boot uses both and merges them
The app fails with a duplicate property error
questions.explanation: Environment variables have higher priority than application.properties, so any property can be overridden from outside.

questions.question: The app fails with password authentication failed for user library_app. What should you check?
options: The @Entity annotation on the class
The port number of the embedded Tomcat
The user name and password against what PostgreSQL has for that user
The name of the main class
questions.explanation: This message comes from the server and means the login does not match what it stores.

questions.question: A new user cannot create tables and sees permission denied for schema public on a recent PostgreSQL. What is a good fix?
options: Make that user the owner of the database, or grant it the needed rights
Switch ddl-auto to none and hope
Add spring-boot-h2console to the pom
Use the ORDINAL enum type
questions.explanation: Recent PostgreSQL versions no longer let every user create tables in the public schema, so the user needs ownership or grants.
